title: Circle Area and Circumference Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Adjust the radius of a circle and watch the circumference and area formulas update with the values substituted, then compare what happens to each measurement when the radius doubles.

educational.topic: Circumference and area of a circle
learningObjectives: Students will be able to calculate the circumference and area of a circle from its radius and analyze how a change in radius affects each measurement.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with worked substitution into the formulas
keyQuestions: Why does doubling the radius double the circumference but quadruple the area?
How are the radius and the diameter related?
Which grows faster as the radius increases, C or A?
commonMisconceptions: Doubling the radius doubles the area (it multiplies the area by four).
Circumference and area use the same units (one is a length, the other is a square measure).
πr² means (πr)² (only the radius is squared).
assessmentOpportunities: Students find the circumference and area of a circle with a radius the MicroSim cannot show (for example r = 25 cm) and explain, without recalculating, how the area compares with the area at r = 12.5 cm.
